title: Urban Solar Energy & Shade Simulation
description: Users manage a virtual city's solar energy grid by placing and configuring shadow-casting structures and tinted lens filters across city blocks. Adjust sun position, lens tint properties, and shadow mesh orientations to maximize solar panel output while keeping pedestrian zones shaded. The simulation enforces energy conservation laws, couples multiple inputs, and supports full undo/redo of all actions.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing an urban solar energy and shade simulation. Load VirtualCity.glb as the base city environment centered at origin. Load ShadowmappableMesh.glb as relocatable shade structures the user can clone and place onto city blocks (up to 5 instances). Load SunglassesKhronos.glb as a giant atmospheric lens filter that hovers above the city and can be repositioned and rotated to selectively filter sunlight onto districts below. Camera: OrbitControls, initial position (0,40,60) looking at origin. Lighting: one DirectionalLight acting as the sun with shadow mapping enabled (2048 shadow map, shadow camera frustum covering the city). Add ambient light at 0.2 intensity. Renderer must have shadowMap enabled (PCFSoftShadowMap). All meshes cast and receive shadows. Interactions (10-14 steps): 1) Click a toolbar button to spawn a ShadowmappableMesh clone at a default position. 2) Drag-and-drop shade structures on the XZ plane using raycasting. 3) Right-click a shade structure to rotate it 45 degrees. 4) Use a slider (0-360) to orbit the DirectionalLight around the city (sun azimuth), updating shadow positions in real time. 5) Use a second slider to adjust sun elevation (10-80 degrees). 6) Click the sunglasses model to select it, then drag to reposition it on XZ plane above the city. 7) Use a tint slider (0-1) that adjusts the sunglasses lens opacity/color, which modulates light intensity passing through (multiply directional light intensity by 1-tint*0.7). 8) A real-time energy readout panel shows total solar energy collected by 4 rooftop solar zones (simple planes on buildings) calculated as base irradiance minus shadow occlusion percentage via raycasting from sun direction. 9) A shade comfort score counts how many of 6 pedestrian zone sample points are in shadow. 10) Conservation law: total energy equals solar input; energy is either collected, blocked by shade structures, or filtered by lens. Display this balance bar. 11) Undo button reverts last action (placement, rotation, slider change) using a state history stack. 12) Redo button re-applies undone actions. Store up to 30 history states. Use a HUD overlay div for sliders, buttons, energy readout, shade score, and conservation bar. All GLB models loaded via GLTFLoader.
